question: Which version-1 cross-language numeric contract should P1 adopt for tagged REAL values and integer control fields so Python runtime acceptance, JSON schemas, fixed wire semantics, and the intended Rust mapping agree?

options.summary: Adopt IEEE-754 binary64 REAL canonicalization plus fixed i64/u64 integer bounds.
options.consequence: Under the REAL tag, accept finite built-in Python int or float values except bool, canonicalize to built-in float/binary64, and reject conversion overflow or nonfinite results as ValueError; document possible binary64 rounding of large integer-valued REAL inputs. Map ContractValue INTEGER to signed 64-bit and nonnegative schema/revision/iteration control fields to unsigned 64-bit, enforce the same JSON-Schema bounds, and return a structured revision-overflow firing error at u64 maximum. This uses Rust primitive i64/u64/f64 types and adds no dependency.

options.summary: Preserve float-only Python REAL construction and distinguish integer versus real JSON lexical forms; use fixed i64/u64 integer bounds.
options.consequence: Keep exact built-in float-only REAL construction, require a project decoder/serializer to preserve and enforce JSON integer-versus-real lexical form beyond ordinary JSON Schema type checking, map integers to i64/u64, and add structured revision overflow. This creates a stricter wire-decoder obligation and leaves JSON Schema alone unable to express the full REAL distinction.

options.summary: Use arbitrary-precision integers and a separately specified exact-decimal REAL representation.
options.consequence: Introduce arbitrary-precision Rust numeric dependencies and replace or extend the current JSON numeric representation with an exact-decimal contract. This broadens dependency, interoperability, schema, and implementation scope and requires additional design and verification before P1 can close.
Keep P1 blocked and unaccepted. No successor, SNAKES adapter, persistence implementation, concrete workflow, or scientific execution may begin.

recommendation: Option A. It makes the public contract directly expressible with standard Python, JSON Schema, and Rust primitive types; resolves integer-valued JSON numbers under the REAL tag without a hidden custom decoder; defines explicit bounded control fields and revision overflow; introduces no dependency; and remains adequate for P1 routing/control values, which own no scientific numerical tolerance or high-precision payload semantics.
blocked_scope: P1 numeric wire-contract correction, complete Python/schema/Rust agreement, parent verification, P1 final-acceptance checkpoint, P1 closure, and every P2-P11 or production/scientific successor action.
safe_scope: Read-only inspection of P1 source, tests, schemas, fixtures, documentation, and retained review evidence. Deterministic corrections unrelated to the protected numeric choice remain permitted if newly discovered, followed by revalidation and review. The human-authorized deterministic P1 test-ownership correction and its non-numeric validation artifacts are also permitted; they must not change production source, schemas, fixtures, dependencies, or the protected numeric contract.
authorized_scope: P1 Option A numeric wire-contract correction only: binary64 REAL canonicalization from finite built-in int/float excluding bool; fixed i64 ContractValue INTEGER bounds; fixed u64 bounds for nonnegative schema, revision, iteration, and related control fields; matching JSON-Schema bounds; structured revision-overflow firing error; corresponding focused tests, schemas/fixtures, documentation, independent reviews, parent verification, and creation of a separate P1 final-acceptance checkpoint. No arithmetic iteration-index advancement, SNAKES adapter, persistence, P2-P11 work, production/scientific execution, or P1 closure is authorized by this decision.
